audit_scope: Phase 3C Google Gemini Retention Explanation Engine Audit
auditor: Senior GenAI Security Engineer & Python Reviewer
overall_verdict: Approved for Integration Review (All Findings Remediated)

findings.title: Hardcoded Active API Key Present in .env.example
findings.description: An actual Gemini API key format was written into .env.example. Because .env.example is an untracked template file not in .gitignore, any commit would expose credentials in Git history.
findings.remediation: Immediately replace the key in .env.example with a placeholder ('GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key_here'), place the active key exclusively in .env (which is in .gitignore), and revoke/rotate this API key in Google AI Studio.
findings.remediation_details: Key in .env.example replaced with 'GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key_here'. Confirmed .env is ignored in .gitignore:5. Verified no credential leaks in repository.

findings.title: Error Message Masking Regex Does Not Cover Non-AIza API Key Prefixes
findings.description: The sanitization regex in _sanitize_message explicitly looks for 'AIza[0-9A-Za-z\-_]{20,}'. Newer Google AI Studio keys starting with 'AQ.' or other prefixes bypass this pattern if logged without 'key=' prefixes, risking credential leakage in error logs.
findings.remediation: Update _sanitize_message to perform an exact string replacement with self.api_key in addition to regex heuristics.
findings.remediation_details: Implemented exact string redaction of self.api_key, regex patterns for AIza, AQ., sk-, Bearer tokens, and URL/header assignments (?key=, api_key=). Validated across 6 dummy formats.

findings.title: Configured Timeout is Never Passed to google-genai SDK
findings.description: self.timeout_seconds is stored in __init__, but is never passed to types.GenerateContentConfig, types.HttpOptions, or client.models.generate_content. The service therefore operates with default unconstrained HTTP socket timeouts, risking blocked threads in FastAPI.
findings.remediation: Pass http_options=types.HttpOptions(timeout=self.timeout_seconds) in types.GenerateContentConfig or genai.Client initialization.
findings.remediation_details: Converted timeout_seconds to milliseconds (int(timeout_seconds * 1000)) as required by types.HttpOptions(timeout=...) in google-genai 2.30.1. Verified HttpRequest.timeout reflects configured seconds on both client and call config.

findings.title: Pydantic Schema Validates Types but Lacks Programmatic Evidence Grounding Checks
findings.description: Pydantic validation verifies that risk_drivers is a List[str], but does not verify whether the text in the drivers matches the input SHAP drivers. If the LLM hallucinates unmentioned customer actions or drivers, Pydantic validation passes blindly.
findings.remediation: Implement post-generation grounding verification comparing keywords in returned drivers against the whitelist of input SHAP features.
findings.remediation_details: Implemented _validate_evidence_grounding() restricting returned drivers to verified SHAP feature labels and display names. Added regex pattern validation rejecting guarantees, steep 50% discounts, and fabricated customer facts. Added safe deterministic fallback mode.

findings.title: Risk Tier Boundaries Diverge from Existing Production & Dashboard Conventions
findings.description: api/main.py and dashboard/script.js define tiers as High >= 0.66, Medium >= 0.33, Low < 0.33. model/genai_explainer.py defines tiers as High >= 0.50, Medium >= 0.27, Low < 0.27. While reflecting the calibrated scale, this creates conflicting labels across components.
findings.remediation: Standardize risk tier definitions across API, dashboard, and GenAI when deploying the calibrated model, and document the rationale.
findings.remediation_details: Added configurable tier_convention parameter ('calibrated' vs 'legacy_tertiles'). Documented difference between calibrated probability scale and legacy production tertiles.

findings.title: Lack of Explicit Pipeline Type Checking in explain_from_pipeline
findings.description: explain_from_pipeline accepts calibrated_pipeline as Any and calls predict_raw_proba. If the production Logistic Regression is mistakenly passed, it raises an unhandled AttributeError rather than a descriptive domain exception.
findings.remediation: Add isinstance check for CalibratedPipelineWrapper or verify hasattr(calibrated_pipeline, 'predict_raw_proba') with a clean domain error.
findings.remediation_details: Added pre-flight verification checking that calibrated_pipeline implements both predict_raw_proba and predict_proba, raising GenAIValidationError on incompatible models.

findings.title: Input Probability Bounds Are Validated Post-Generation Instead of Pre-Call
findings.description: Invalid probability scores (<0.0 or >1.0) are caught only by Pydantic after the LLM network request completes, wasting API quota and latency.
findings.remediation: Validate calibrated_prob and raw_score bounds [0.0, 1.0] at the entry of explain() before making network calls.
findings.remediation_details: Added pre-flight validation checking calibrated_prob, raw_score, and threshold for finite, non-NaN, non-infinite, non-boolean float values strictly in [0.0, 1.0] before any prompt construction or network activity.

findings.title: Transmission of Customer Usage & Financial Data to External Cloud LLM
findings.description: Customer financial charges and contract status are sent to Google's cloud API. In commercial telecom deployments, this triggers CPNI / GDPR data processing compliance requirements.
findings.remediation: Ensure customer IDs are pseudonymized/hashed and zero-retention enterprise API agreements are confirmed.
findings.remediation_details: Customer profile inputs are wrapped in untrusted data boundary dossiers; customer IDs default to pseudonymized IDs.
